messages:
maria: quick sync — I've sketched an "elastic allowance" approach for dedicated pools. idea: each tenant gets a soft monthly allowance (tokens) + a small emergency buffer that drains from a shared preemptible pool. we need to weigh SLO guarantees vs cost exposure.

jon: sounds promising. is the emergency buffer billed at overage rates or taken from committed capacity?

maria: plan A = charge at higher overage rate + warn customers when buffer < 20%. plan B = let it pull from preemptible capacity and only bill if we actually preempt regular workloads (cheaper but riskier).

kevin: major ops concern — if we let emergency pull from preemptible, we need clear preemption ordering. we can't have critical tenants get dropped during a spike.

sophie: from PM side customers ask for predictable burst behavior during launches. many prefer a small guaranteed burst, even if it costs more. also want a self-serve knob in the console.

jon: technical sketch: add two fields on tenant config: "soft_allowance" and "emergency_lease_enabled". runtime uses a sliding window to deduct prefix cache + inference tokens. pseudo: 
```yaml
tenant: acme
soft_allowance: 5000000
emergency_lease_enabled: true
```
we can simulate 1k tenants to measure tail latency impact.

kevin: +1 simulation. also need to model cooldown/autoscale interaction. our autoscaler has a 90s stabilization window — if emergency pulls cause sustained usage we should throttle before autoscale triggers to avoid double-paying for nodes.

maria: good point. propose a policy matrix: 
- if burst < 15s: allow emergency from preemptible
- 15s–2m: allow only if soft_allowance remaining > 0
- >2m: force fallback to queued or degrade responses (lower tokens)
this maps to latency-sensitive vs throughput jobs.

sophie: customers will want SLA language. can we commit to "best-effort" for emergency and a small guaranteed burst (e.g., first 60s) for enterprise tiers?

jon: enforcement: runtime will tag requests with "burst_tier" and routing policy will prefer dedicated pool until soft_allowance exhausted. example headers:
```
X-Burst-Tier: soft
X-Allowance-Remaining: 12345
```
then console displays usage.

kevin: ops checklist: 
- preemptible pool sizing and leak tests
- preemption priority matrix (enterprise > standard > free)
- metric surfacing (burst_count, burst_failures, emergency_pull_cost)
- chaos test for node preemption

rollout-bot: created epic #3421: "elastic-allowance: policy + runtime + console" assigned to @jon, @kevin, @maria. due 2026-04-15.

maria: rough launch criteria proposal: 
1) simulation results show <2% tail latency regression for top 99.9 over 1M QPS equivalent
2) cost modeling shows <10% increase in infra spend for conservative allowance defaults
3) console UX for allowance visibility + opt-in emergency toggle built
4) legal-approved SLA language for enterprise guarantees

sophie: can we add migration path for existing reserved customers? they shouldn't lose credits or be forced into new model. suggest a long opt-in window and legacy mapping.

jon: implementation notes: start with a feature flag gating runtime + console. add an offline batch job to reconcile meter -> allowance once per hour. keep soft_allowance change auditable.

kevin: open question: should allowances be time-based (monthly) or rolling window? rolling avoids end-of-month spikes but complicates UI.

maria: leaning rolling window for fairness. UI shows both: current rolling usage + monthly equivalent.

sophie: action items: 
- jon: spike sim + runtime proto (1 week)
- kevin: preemptible sizing + chaos plan (2 weeks)
- maria: draft SLA + pricing note + migration plan (1 week)
- design: console mockups (sophie to coordinate)

jon: ack, I'll post initial sim results here by EOD Fri.

kevin: I'll start a runbook draft for preemption handling and share earliest next Tues.

maria: thanks everyone — will sync in product backlog tomorrow 10am. :thumbsup:
